# Client priority to delivery week

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | draft for team review |


Every card the client put on the prioritization bands of the kickoff Lucid
board, in the order they put them, against the delivery week it lands in.
One row per card. This is the artifact the feature prioritization workshop
argues over and the one the team tracks against afterwards.

Two things this page will not do. It will not invent a delivery week for a
card the plan of record does not schedule, and it will not invent a Jira key.
Blank cells are real answers.

## Where the ordering comes from

The bands and the order of cards inside them are read off the live board, not
off this repo. The repo records band membership for twelve items in the board
mapping table of [Backlog: Epics and Features](/backlog-epics), and the Lucid
board manifest at `product/design/lucid-board/manifest.md` states plainly that
it holds no export of the board. So position was taken from the board itself
on 2026-08-24.

Rank is the card's left-to-right position inside its band rectangle. That is
the only ordering the board carries. The client did not number the cards, so
rank here means reading order, not a stack rank the client signed.

The three band captions, verbatim from the board:

- GREEN. `FIRST - CARRIES THE DAILY LOOP`
- ORANGE. `NEXT - THE REAL CONVERSATION - what earns a sprint slot?`
- GRAY. `OUTSIDE THESE 8 WEEKS - each has a later home, none are dropped`

### Four ways the live board and this repo disagree

Named here rather than reconciled, because the board is the client's and this
repo is ours.

1. The board carries 17 cards. The repo's board mapping table carries 12. Two
   things account for the gap. Auth and Onboarding are two cards on the board
   and one row, "Auth plus onboarding", in the repo. And four cards are on the
   board and absent from the repo table entirely: Sharing personal, Reactions,
   picking multiple pictures and grouping them, and comments. 12 rows, plus
   the split, plus those four, is 17.
2. Analytics instrumentation sits in the GREEN band on the board. The repo
   maps it to the ORANGE band. The delivery answer is the same either way,
   because nothing in the orange band has a slot and nothing green schedules
   it, but the band label needs settling in the room.
3. Reactions is the same disagreement in the other direction. The card sits in
   the ORANGE band on the board. The repo has it as E05-F6, banded GREEN,
   sized at 2 backend-days inside E05. Here the label does change the answer,
   because E05 completes in week 8 and an orange card does not get a week at
   all. This one has to be settled in the room, not on this page.
4. The repo's board mapping table has no ordering in it at all, so nothing on
   this page's Rank column can be checked against the repo. It can only be
   checked against the board.

## The weeks

Week numbers are the eight build weeks. Sprint boundaries fall on Wednesdays,
so a week label is approximate at every boundary. Dates and phases are the
confirmed calendar on [Timeline and Milestones](/timeline-and-milestones).

| Week | Monday | Phase | Demo |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-08-24 | Shape | |
| 2 | 2026-08-31 | Shape ends 09-01, sprint 1 starts 09-02 | M0 Shape readout, Wed 2026-09-02 |
| 3 | 2026-09-07 | Sprint 1 | |
| 4 | 2026-09-14 | Sprint 1 | M1 sprint 1 demo, Wed 2026-09-16. The anchor |
| 5 | 2026-09-21 | Sprint 2 | |
| 6 | 2026-09-28 | Sprint 2 | M2 sprint 2 demo, Wed 2026-09-30 |
| 7 | 2026-10-05 | Sprint 3 | |
| 8 | 2026-10-12 | Sprint 3 | M3 sprint 3 demo, Wed 2026-10-14 |

One caveat on every week below. The lane arithmetic these weeks rest on was
computed on 2026-08-20 and the delivery roster has moved since. The iOS lane
lost its first Shape week and gains a second engineer inside week 1, and the
2026-08-24 standup records both. Whether that moves week 4 is a sprint 1
planning question and this page does not answer it.

Three states are used below rather than one date, because a card does not
arrive whole.

- **Underway.** Work has started and there is nothing a person can use.
- **Demonstrable.** Something works at a demo, and the card is not finished.
- **Complete.** The card is done as the client wrote it.

## The mapping

Delivery weeks come from the milestone statements on
[Timeline and Milestones](/timeline-and-milestones), which is the only place
the plan of record says what is true at each demo. Sprint 1 also has a ranked
queue on [Backlog: Epics and Features](/backlog-epics). Sprint 3 has no
feature assignment anywhere, so no row below claims one.

Every Jira key below was read back from Jira itself on 2026-08-24, one issue
at a time, not derived from anything in this repo. Epics that were not filed
at the moment this page was written carry a blank key and are named in prose
instead.

### GREEN. First, carries the daily loop

| Rank | Card, verbatim from the board | Epic | Jira epic | Underway | Demonstrable | Complete |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Drawing + submit, with submit-to-unlock | E04 | SCRIBL-40 | Week 2 | Week 4 | Week 6 |
| 2 | Daily prompt - curated (Claude) | E03 | SCRIBL-34 | | Week 4 | Week 6 |
| 3 | Auth | E02, the auth half | SCRIBL-27 | | Week 4 | Week 4 |
| 4 | Walls + channels | E05 | SCRIBL-47 | Week 6 | Week 8 | Week 8 |
| 5 | Cloud foundation (AWS, CI/CD, data model) | E01 | SCRIBL-1 | Week 2 | Week 4 | Week 6 |
| 6 | Onboarding + Invited/New user | E02, the onboarding half | SCRIBL-27 | | Week 6 | Not inside the eight weeks |
| 7 | Analytics instrumentation (instrument now, report later) | E08 | SCRIBL-68 | | Not inside the eight weeks | |

Row by row, and what the week rests on.

**1. Drawing + submit.** The canvas engine starts in Shape, 2 of its 5 days,
ink-agnostic so it can run before the six inks are named. Week 4 is the Skia
canvas with the six inks and you can draw on it. Week 6 is submit persisting,
artwork in S3 behind CloudFront, and submit-to-unlock enforced at the data
layer with its bypass test. Week 4 is explicitly not persistence. What you
draw at the anchor demo is not saved.

**2. Daily prompt.** Week 4 puts today's prompt on screen. Week 6 serves it
from the seeded curated set on the real fetch contract rather than the mock.
Note the wording on the card. The kickoff decided prompts stay curated by
Scribl's own program team, with Claude scoped to drafting suggestions for
their review. The card's "(Claude)" is not authorization to generate prompts
at runtime.

**3. Auth.** Week 4, sign in with email and password on a device. Complete at
week 4 for the auth half. Federation is out of this phase.

**4. Walls + channels.** Week 6 is backend-first and deliberately not
demonstrable end to end. Week 8 is the wall grid, a response detail, and
server-side channel isolation with its regression gate. No dashboard or stats
card if E05-F5 stays cut.

**5. Cloud foundation.** Week 2 is the API contract, a running mock server,
the schema drafted and reviewed, and the CDK stack synthesizing locally.
Nothing is deployed at week 2. Week 4 is a hosted API and a relational
database in a real AWS environment. Week 6 adds media storage and delivery
and the rest of the observability floor.

**6. Onboarding + Invited/New user.** Guided onboarding screens 1 to 8 land
at week 6. The invited-user half does not land inside the eight weeks,
because the invite path is unfunded (Q8). A second person reaches a wall only
by a route nobody has funded. This card is the clearest split between what
the client asked for and what the eight weeks buy.

**7. Analytics instrumentation.** No week inside the eight weeks. The sprint 3
milestone says there are no analytics events at the end of it. The board puts
this card in GREEN and it is the one green card with no slot at all, which
makes it the sharpest thing on this page to discuss in the room.

### ORANGE. Next, the real conversation, what earns a sprint slot

None of these has a slot inside the eight weeks. That is not a sequencing
choice that a different order would fix. Green alone is 128 lane-days against
108 available, and green plus orange is 155 against 108.

| Rank | Card, verbatim from the board | Epic | Jira epic | Delivery week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Push notifications (the daily nudge) | E09 | | Not inside the eight weeks |
| 2 | Moderation (fail-safe) | E10 | | Not inside the eight weeks |
| 3 | Streaks + progression | E11 | | Not inside the eight weeks |
| 4 | Sharing personal | E12 | not filed | Not sourced |
| 5 | Reactions | E05-F6, reactions post-unlock only | SCRIBL-47, the parent epic | Not stated |

E09, E10 and E11 were not filed in Jira when this page was written, so their
key cells are blank rather than predicted. "Sharing personal" is now E12,
Sharing a response, and a wall, as a document, opened 2026-08-25 and not yet
in Jira. It has a decomposition, five features, but no delivery week, so the
row still needs the workshop to rank it.

Reactions reads "Not stated" and that is the accurate answer, not a hedge. The
sprint 2 milestone says there are no reactions at week 6. The sprint 3
milestone does not mention them in either column, so the plan of record neither
schedules them nor rules them out. Because the repo bands E05-F6 green inside
an epic that completes in week 8, this is the one card where the band argument
in the room decides whether the number below moves from six to seven.

### GRAY. Outside these 8 weeks, each has a later home, none are dropped

| Rank | Card, verbatim from the board | Epic | Jira epic | Later home |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | App Store readiness + compliance -> release phase | E14 | | The release phase after sprint 3, gated on Q56 |
| 2 | re:Invent event wall -> its own scope + funding call | E15 | | Its own scope and funding call, tracked as Q21 |
| 3 | Under-13 / COPPA Family edition -> after launch planning | E16 | | Post-launch planning, tracked as Q32 |

Both gray cards now have a backlog item. Card 4, picking multiple pictures
and grouping them, is E12-F2, the deferred multi-picture extension of E12
Sharing a response, and a wall, as a document. It is not the parked keepsake
feature E18-F4; that one composes a keepsake from wall tiles and stays parked
on Q19 with no recorded relationship to this card. Card 5, comments, is E13,
Comments, with the wall creator as moderator, opened 2026-08-25. It still
shows here in the gray table because that is where the live board places it,
but the epic itself carries an orange band, not gray, per the 2026-08-25
prioritization session.

## The burn-up

Reporting on this engagement is a burn-up, not a burn-down. Scope is not
fixed, and the board is the proof of that: it grew from twelve cards to
seventeen between the kickoff and today. A burn-down would draw a line to
zero against a scope nobody agreed to freeze.

So the chart counts cards landed, cumulative, against the number of cards on
the board. The scope line moves up when the client adds a card. It never
moves down.

| Demo | Week | Cards demonstrable or better, cumulative | Cards complete, cumulative | Cards on the board |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 Shape readout | 2 | 0 | 0 | 17 |
| M1 sprint 1 | 4 | 4 | 1 | 17 |
| M2 sprint 2 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 17 |
| M3 sprint 3 | 8 | 6 | 5 | 17 |

Six of seventeen client cards land inside the eight weeks. Five of those six
are complete by the last demo. Ten have no week and one, Reactions, has no
stated answer either way. Every one of the eleven has a reason on this page
rather than a shrug.

The two gates on the anchor demo hold this whole table up. Q5, the Apple
Developer account, decides whether there is a build a tester can install.
Q17 with Q49 decide whose AWS account and whose money, and nothing in the
backend lane deploys until they close. If either is open on 2026-09-02, week
4 loses most of its column.
